newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Saipem falls sharply in Milan.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Saipem falls sharply in Milan.

text.p: Saipem, the oilfield services arm of Italian energy group ENI, was sharply down in active trade on a generally weaker Milan bourse following press reports of flat 1996 profits, traders said.
The reports forecast Saipem's full-year profit in line with 1995's 168.6 billion lire, which was up 11 percent on 1994.
Saipem shares, which also saw falls on Tuesday, were down 6.52 percent at 1300 GMT at 6,565 lire in volume of nearly four million shares after a session low at 6,450 lire.

"I don't think Saipem's current performance is justified by fundamentals," said Claudia Vignati, analyst at Credito Italiano. "The company had already said that 1996 profit would not show the same rate of growth as in 1995."
She forecast 1996 net profit of 178 billion lire, adding that the stock was "interesting" at 6,500 to 6,700 lire.
Elena Sottanella, analist at Pasfin brokers, said she was neutral on the stock, noting the weekend press reports had forecast a peak in Saipem investments next year.
"Its 1997 investments should be around 400 billion lire, which will clearly impact profit figures," she said.
Saipem shares were around 3,500 lire at the start of 1996, touching a high of 7,920 lire on November 15.
